units.title: Shunting signal
units.text: A signal used for low-speed movements within a yard rather than normal main-line running, authorizing a defined shunting movement when displayed.

units.title: Entering between vehicles
units.text: Before a worker enters between coupled rail vehicles, the movement must be stopped, the handbrake secured and the driver or shunter must confirm that no movement will occur.

units.title: Shunting radio
units.text: The ground shunter gives movement instructions over the dedicated yard radio channel, and the driver repeats the instruction before moving the consist.

units.title: Reduced-visibility speed
units.text: During heavy fog, shunting speed is reduced because staff may have less time to identify points, vehicles and people on the movement route.

units.title: Hand points
units.text: The shunter checks the blade position and target route, operates the lever and confirms the points are fully home before authorizing the movement.
